checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add a time-reversal score transform

impact_assessment.why: Reversal is a basic compositional device that turns an existing phrase into a new one without writing notes by hand.
impact_assessment.benefits: reverse mirrors every note's start around the score's end while preserving duration, pitch, velocity, pan and envelopes; applying it twice is an exact identity.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: note order and all non-start fields must be untouched so double reversal is byte-identical; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure reverse module with field-preservation and double-identity tests, a CLI command writing canonical source, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 132 tests green; double reversal is byte-identical in source and audio
Task 'coda-reverse' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: d0ccd95039e2148ac16cb59494a831c2dfdb0e36

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add deterministic auto-pan

impact_assessment.why: Stereo output exists but the image is static unless every note sets its own pan; an LFO sweep gives motion without editing scores.
impact_assessment.benefits: --autopan-rate and --autopan-depth apply an equal-power stereo sweep to any render, with depth 0 preserving existing bytes.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: depth 0 must be byte-identical to golden vectors; gains must stay bounded; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure autopan module with identity, LFO-phase and bounded-gain tests, wire two CLI options into the shared audio helper, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 137 tests green; autopan LFO balance and zero-depth identity pinned, audio options grouped to satisfy clippy
Task 'coda-autopan' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: 8986af3ad161fdffd617fbc8b3dd94c241e575ab

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add note-start quantization

impact_assessment.why: Variation and live-style input can leave notes slightly off-grid; a tools step is needed to snap them to a chosen rhythmic grid.
impact_assessment.benefits: quantize snaps note starts to the nearest multiple of a grid while preserving durations and all other fields, with an exact identity when already on-grid.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: invalid grids must fail clearly; non-start fields must be untouched; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure quantize module with snapping, identity and preservation tests, a CLI command writing canonical source, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 142 tests green; quantization snapping, idempotence and field preservation pinned by byte tests
Task 'coda-quantize' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: 50b3f572447202e2f6e2be150ae506dd2608c35e

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add WAV frame reversal

impact_assessment.why: Reverse audio is a standard sound-design tool and the score-level reverse already exists; the audio counterpart completes the pair.
impact_assessment.benefits: reverse-wav flips sample order in a Coda WAV with a rebuilt header, is idempotent when applied twice, and needs no external editor.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: invalid WAVs must fail clearly and double reversal must be byte-identical; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure reversal module with exact frame-order and double-identity tests, a CLI command, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 146 tests green; frame-order reversal and double-reverse byte identity pinned
Task 'coda-wav-reverse' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: 5b76d0346f709b59ac96dd4473e90593c78ae02c

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add deterministic WAV mixing

impact_assessment.why: join composes sections sequentially; layering tracks in parallel needs a mixer to be useful as a small studio tool.
impact_assessment.benefits: mix overlays two Coda WAVs with a gain on the second input, clamping safely and producing deterministic bytes.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: sample rates must match or fail clearly, silence plus a track with zero gain must be an identity, and output length must be the longer input; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure mix module with identity, length and clamping byte tests, a CLI command, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 151 tests green; mixing gain, clamping, longer-length and zero-gain identity pinned by byte tests
Task 'coda-mix' completed successfully.
checkpoints.head: 543d3a84f0070dd9d209a7632d883f0f5ecaa44c

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add seeded humanize timing/velocity jitter

impact_assessment.why: Perfectly quantized scores sound mechanical; a bounded seeded jitter gives a more natural performance without randomizing everything.
impact_assessment.benefits: humanize applies small reproducible timing and velocity variations with amount 0 as an exact identity, writing ordinary editable source.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: velocity must stay in range and starts non-negative; amount 0 must be byte-identical; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure humanize module with identity, determinism and bounds tests, a CLI command, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 157 tests green; humanize seeded identity and explicit-rest serialization verified
Task 'coda-humanize' completed successfully.

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Plan and add scale-degree transposition

impact_assessment.why: Chromatic transposition shifts every note by semitones; moving a melody by scale degrees within a key needs a different transform to stay diatonic.
impact_assessment.benefits: diatonic transposes notes by scale steps in major/minor/pentatonic/chromatic scales, preserving key membership and all non-pitch fields.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: steps 0 must be an identity, notes outside the scale must map deterministically, and output must remain in range; dependency: std only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add a pure diatonic module with identity, octave and key-membership tests, a CLI command, then run cargo gates and aikit check --strict.

checkpoints.description: 5/5 AIKit gates passed; 163 tests green; diatonic identity, octave walk, key membership and scale flag pinned by byte tests
